goal: Second discovery wave across five domains, at a raised target of 8-10 records per domain rather than 5.
scope: Five domains: photo, health, baby-pet, wearables, office. 49 records to 68.

domains._note: counts are of files written; several are rejections, which do not publish to a domain page

incident: All five agents were terminated mid-run by a session usage limit. Each had written records to disk before dying. No file was truncated mid-write and no agent had touched anything outside data/devices/, so the partial output was recoverable in full. The wave was reviewed and committed from disk rather than re-run.
findings: Six of nineteen records are rejections and five of those six have no alternative to offer. The gap is real rather than a filing error: verified subscription-free pet trackers, pet feeders, drones and cellular trail cameras are not known to exist. Recorded as open questions on the rejections rather than papered over.

Two agents independently hit the same class of problem — the radios enum had no honest tag for what they were looking at — and both used the nearest wrong value while flagging it in open_questions rather than silently fudging. That is the behaviour the principles ask for and it worked without prompting.

system_gaps_found.gap: fi-series-3-plus was rejected on a fact its own two cited sources contradicted each other about: one said the collar will not enable at all without a membership, the other that it loses out-of-range GPS specifically. A REJECT is the most damaging verdict to get wrong.
system_gaps_found.fix: Narrowed the rejection to the claim both sources support and that retail listings independently corroborate — the hardware is sold only bundled with a prepaid membership term. Added two VERIFIER rules: never reject on a fact your own sources disagree about, and check how the thing is sold, because a REJECT is a claim about a purchase.

system_gaps_found.gap: radios enum still had no tag for a 2.4 GHz proprietary FHSS point-to-point link (not 802.11) or for a 125-134 kHz ISO 11785 pet-microchip reader (not 13.56 MHz NFC).
system_gaps_found.fix: Added proprietary_24ghz and rfid_lf; retagged infant-optics-dxr-8-pro and sureflap-microchip-pet-door.

system_gaps_found.gap: Two records cited fccid.io search-results pages while naming specific grant IDs in the supports text.
system_gaps_found.fix: Repointed at the grant pages. Search URLs remain correct where the finding IS an absence of grant — there the search is the evidence.

system_gaps_found.gap: Three published records carried vendor_risk above 0 with no backing entry in data/vendors.json, meaning the score came from the model's impression of the company. Found during this review, fixed in a separate commit.
system_gaps_found.fix: Researched and added eufy, Ring and Withings to the ledger; Withings did not survive at 2 and was corrected to 1. validate.mjs now fails any nonzero vendor_risk without a matching ledger entry.

honest_limitations: Two rejections were spot-checked against primary sources (fi-series-3-plus, petlibro-granary-camera-feeder); the other seventeen records were reviewed for schema, source class, and tier-table consistency but not re-derived.

petlibro-granary-camera-feeder is rejected on a documented account-at-setup step while its own open question concedes the deciding fact — whether the unit's touch panel can schedule feeds with no app — is unresolved. PETLIBRO documents exactly that capability for the non-camera sibling (AF005/AF006) and not for the camera model. The rejection stands on the vendor's published setup process, but the sibling is the better catalog candidate and is not yet researched.
surprises: The most useful thing this wave produced was not a record but a discovered failure mode. Agents are good at finding sources and bad at noticing when two of their own sources disagree — the contradiction sat in plain sight inside a single record's own open_questions field while the rejection_reason asserted the stronger claim anyway. Worth a CRITIC pass on whether any other published record does the same.
